pages.text: A cruel king in Egypt made God's people, the Israelites, work very hard. One mother hid her baby boy to keep him safe.
When she could not hide him any longer, she made a basket boat and set it in the river. His big sister Miriam watched over him.
The king's daughter found the baby and loved him. She named him Moses. Miriam found his own mother to take care of him.
Moses grew up in the king's palace, but he never forgot God's people. He saw how hard they worked, and he wanted to help.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: God watched over baby Moses and kept him safe. God watches over every one of us, too.

pages.text: Moses was a shepherd now, caring for sheep far from Egypt. One day he saw a bush on fire, but it did not burn up.
God spoke from the bush: "Moses, take off your sandals. This is holy ground. I have seen my people suffer. I will send you to set them free."
Moses said, "Who am I? I cannot speak well." God said, "I will be with you." God also sent Moses' brother Aaron to help him.
Moses trusted God and went back to Egypt with Aaron. God is always with His people, and He is always with us.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: Moses felt too small for a big job, but God said, "I will be with you." God helps us when things feel too big.

pages.text: Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh, "Let God's people go!" But Pharaoh said no. So God sent signs to show His power, and still Pharaoh would not listen.
God told each family to share a special meal of roasted lamb and flat bread. They marked their doorways to show they trusted God.
That night, God passed over the homes with marked doors and kept those families safe. This is why it is called the Passover.
At last Pharaoh said, "Go!" The Israelites packed up and left Egypt. They were free after many long years as slaves.
God told His people to celebrate the Passover every year to remember how He saved them. One day, Jesus would be called the Lamb of God.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: At Mass, we remember how Jesus saves us, just as the Israelites remembered how God saved them at the Passover.

pages.text: The Israelites came to a big sea, and Pharaoh's army was chasing them! The people were scared. Moses said, "Do not be afraid. God will save us."
A tall cloud stood between the people and the army all night. Moses stretched his staff out over the sea.
God sent a strong wind, and the water split apart! The people walked across on dry ground with walls of water on both sides.
When everyone was safe on the other side, Miriam played her tambourine. The people sang, "Thank you, God! You have saved us!"

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: When the people were afraid, God made a way for them. We can trust God when we are scared.

pages.text: In the desert, the people were hungry and grumbled. But God said, "I will send bread from heaven for you."
Each morning, white flakes called manna covered the ground. The people gathered just enough for each day and thanked God.
Then God called Moses up Mount Sinai. The mountain shook with thunder, and a cloud covered the top. God was very near.
God gave Moses ten rules, the Ten Commandments, written on stone. They show us how to love God and how to love one another.
The rules say: love God most of all, keep Sunday holy, respect your parents, tell the truth, and be kind and fair to everyone.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: God gives us the Ten Commandments to show us how to love Him and our neighbors. Jesus said the greatest commandment is to love God and love others.

pages.text: Moses stayed on the mountain a long time. The people got tired of waiting and said to Aaron, "Make us a god we can see!"
Aaron collected their gold and made a golden calf. The people bowed down to it instead of God. They forgot that God had just saved them.
Moses came down and saw the calf. He was very sad. The people had done wrong, so Moses prayed and asked God to forgive them.
God listened to Moses and forgave His people. God is always ready to forgive when we are truly sorry.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: Only God is worth our deepest love. When we choose wrong, we can say we are sorry, and God forgives us.
